name: GET /api/leadflow/analytics/source-quality - the sources nobody wants to see
description:
High-volume low-conversion sources, surfaced rather than filtered (b7eceb85-6dd9-4335-b950-ff0cf1de6822#AC2). filtered_out is returned as an explicit zero: every source appears in all_sources, and poor_quality is a ranking over that same set. SOP §20 forbids hiding poor-quality sources and the instinct runs the other way - a source with 400 leads and 2 meetings makes the dashboard look bad, so somebody adds a minimum-conversion filter, and that filter is how the channel keeps its budget.

CAMPAIGN NUMBERS RECONCILE WITH THE SALES DASHBOARD (b7eceb85-6dd9-4335-b950-ff0cf1de6822#AC3) because both are computed from the same lead columns and their definitions live in the KPI registry, where a divergence between two tiles showing the same metric name is detected by the reconciliation report rather than discovered in a meeting.

min_volume is a caller parameter with a stated default rather than a hidden constant, so nobody has to guess what "high volume" meant. QA: measured live.

testCases.name: All sources are returned with the poor performers ranked by wasted volume
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
